questions.question: Let (P) be $\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b},\ \boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ with $\boldsymbol{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, and let (D) $\min\{\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\colon\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{c},\ \boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ with $\boldsymbol{y}\in\mathbb{R}^m$ be its dual. Which program is the dual of (D), after writing (D) in standard form, dualizing and cleaning up the signs?
options: $\min\{\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\colon\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{c},\ \boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ with $\boldsymbol{y}\in\mathbb{R}^m$
$\max\{\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{c},\ \boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ with $\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^m$
$\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b},\ \boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ with $\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^n$
$\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{b},\ \boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ with $\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^n$

questions.question: For the primal $\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b},\ \boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$, dualizing its dual via the standard form gives literally $L=\min\{-\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon-\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\geq-\boldsymbol{b},\ \boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$. Which rewriting turns $L$ back into the primal?
options: Replacing $\min(-\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x})$ by $\max\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ and multiplying each constraint by $-1$
Substituting $\boldsymbol{x}=-\boldsymbol{u}$, which removes all minus signs and keeps $\boldsymbol{u}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$
Transposing $-\boldsymbol{A}$ once more, since every dualization transposes the matrix
Replacing $\min$ by $\max$ while keeping $-\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ and the constraints as they are

questions.question: A linear program (P) $\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b},\ \boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ has $m$ constraints and $n$ variables, sign constraints not counted. Which statement about the sizes of its dual (D) and of the dual of (D) is correct?
options: (D) has $m$ constraints and $n$ variables, the sizes of (P), and so does the dual of (D)
(D) has $m$ constraints and $m$ variables, one of each for every constraint of (P)
(D) has $n$ constraints and $m$ variables, and the dual of (D) has these sizes as well
(D) has $n$ constraints and $m$ variables, and the dual of (D) has $m$ constraints and $n$ variables

questions.question: A dual, in standard form $\max\{-\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\colon-\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\leq-\boldsymbol{c},\ \boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ with $\boldsymbol{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, is dualized again. With $\boldsymbol{a}_i^{\top}$ row $i$ of $\boldsymbol{A}$, what do its sign constraints $y_i\geq0$ become?
options: The $n$ sign constraints $x_j\geq0$, since sign constraints are carried over as sign constraints
$m$ further dual variables, one for each of the sign constraints $y_i\geq0$
The $m$ constraints $-\boldsymbol{a}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\geq-b_i$, each with $\geq$ because $y_i\geq0$
The $m$ constraints $-\boldsymbol{a}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\leq-b_i$, since a variable $\geq0$ gives a $\leq$ constraint

questions.question: A student claims that a minimization (M) is the dual of (P) $\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b},\ \boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$. Dualizing means: write in standard form, apply the standard-form rule, clean up the signs. Which of these tests of the claim is valid?
options: Dualize (M) once: if the result is (M) itself, then (M) is the dual of (P)
Dualize (M) once: if the result is not (P), then (M) is not the dual of (P)
Dualize (M) twice: if the result is not (P), then (M) is not the dual of (P)
Count sizes: if (M) and (P) have equally many constraints plus variables, then (M) is the dual of (P)

questions.question: The linear program (M) $\min 4y_1+6y_2+3y_3$ subject to $y_1+2y_2+y_3\geq5$, $3y_1+y_3\geq2$, $\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ is the dual of a linear program in standard form. Since the dual of the dual is the primal, which program is it?
options: $\max 5x_1+2x_2$ subject to $x_1+3x_2\leq4$, $2x_1\leq6$, $x_1+x_2\leq3$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$
$\max 4x_1+6x_2+3x_3$ subject to $x_1+2x_2+x_3\leq5$, $3x_1+x_3\leq2$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$
$\min 5x_1+2x_2$ subject to $x_1+3x_2\geq4$, $2x_1\geq6$, $x_1+x_2\geq3$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$
$\max -5x_1-2x_2$ subject to $x_1+3x_2\leq4$, $2x_1\leq6$, $x_1+x_2\leq3$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$

questions.question: (P) $\max 4x_1+3x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\leq5$, $2x_1+x_2\leq8$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ has optimal solution $(3,2)$ with value $18$, and its dual has optimal solution $\boldsymbol{y}=(2,1)$. What are the optimal solution and optimal value of the uncleaned double dual $\min -4x_1-3x_2$ subject to $-x_1-x_2\geq-5$, $-2x_1-x_2\geq-8$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$?
options: Optimal solution $(3,2)$ with optimal value $18$
Optimal solution $(-3,-2)$ with optimal value $-18$
Optimal solution $(3,2)$ with optimal value $-18$
Optimal solution $(2,1)$ with optimal value $-18$

questions.question: A linear program in standard form has $n=2$ variables and $m=6$ constraints, sign constraints not counted. Suppose the simplex work per iteration grows mainly with the number of constraints. Which statement about solving its dual instead is correct?
options: The dual has $6$ constraints and $2$ variables, so each iteration on it costs more
The dual has $2$ constraints and $6$ variables, so each iteration is cheaper, though the total work need not be
The dual has $2$ constraints and $6$ variables, so the total work is guaranteed to be smaller
Both have $8$ constraints plus variables, so each iteration costs the same, though the number of iterations may differ

questions.question: The primal–dual transformation table has a max column and a min column; for example, a $\leq$ constraint in the max column sits next to a variable $\geq0$ in the min column. Why does the table show at once that dualizing twice returns the original linear program?
options: Both columns list the same items in the same order, so one dualization changes nothing
Each constraint type is paired with the same type, $\leq$ with $\leq$ and $\geq$ with $\geq$
Both dualizations read the table from the max column, so the two sign changes cancel
The dual lies in the other column, and reading the same row back returns the original item

questions.question: A linear program (P) in standard form is dualized $k\geq1$ times in a row, each time writing the current program in standard form first; programs that agree after $\min(-Z)\Longleftrightarrow\max Z$ and multiplying constraints by $-1$ are identified. Let (D) be the dual of (P). Which statement holds for every such (P)?
options: The result is (P) for $k=2$ only; later steps give programs other than (P) and (D)
The result is (P) for every even $k$ and (D) for every odd $k$
The result is (P) only when $k$ is divisible by $4$, since minus signs remain after two steps
The result is (P) for every $k\geq2$, since (P) is reproduced at every step once reached

questions.question: The standard-form rule gives the dual (D) $\min\{\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\colon\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{c},\ \boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ of $\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b},\ \boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$. Why must (D) be rewritten in standard form before the rule is applied to it?
options: It need not be: inserting $\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}$ and $\boldsymbol{c}$ into the rule unchanged already gives back the primal
The rule needs a maximization with $\leq$ constraints; inserting the data of (D) unchanged gives $\geq$ constraints
Only to make the right-hand side nonnegative, so that $\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{0}$ is a feasible starting point
Because the standard form turns $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}$ back into $\boldsymbol{A}$, which the rule needs in order to return the primal

questions.question: The linear program (M) $\min 3y_1+7y_2$ subject to $y_1+2y_2=4$, $3y_1-y_2=1$, $y_1,y_2\geq0$ arose as the dual of a maximization. Using the primal–dual transformation table from the min column, which program is the dual of (M)?
options: $\max 4x_1+x_2$ subject to $x_1+3x_2\leq3$, $2x_1-x_2\leq7$, $x_1,x_2\geq0$
$\max 4x_1+x_2$ subject to $x_1+3x_2=3$, $2x_1-x_2=7$, $x_1,x_2\in\mathbb{R}$
$\max 4x_1+x_2$ subject to $x_1+3x_2\leq3$, $2x_1-x_2\leq7$, $x_1,x_2\in\mathbb{R}$
$\max 4x_1+x_2$ subject to $x_1+3x_2\geq3$, $2x_1-x_2\geq7$, $x_1,x_2\in\mathbb{R}$

questions.question: The dual of $\max 2x_1+5x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\geq3$, $2x_1-x_2\geq-4$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ has variables $y_1,y_2\leq0$; with $\boldsymbol{y}=-\boldsymbol{u}$ it becomes $\max 3u_1-4u_2$ subject to $u_1+2u_2\leq-2$, $u_1-u_2\leq-5$, $\boldsymbol{u}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$. Which program is the dual of this standard-form program?
options: $\min -2x_1-5x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\geq3$, $2x_1-x_2\geq-4$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$
$\min -2x_1-5x_2$ subject to $-x_1-x_2\geq3$, $-2x_1+x_2\geq-4$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$
$\min -2x_1-5x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\geq3$, $2x_1-x_2\geq-4$, $\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{0}$
$\max 2x_1+5x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\leq3$, $2x_1-x_2\leq-4$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$

questions.question: Let (P) be $\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b},\ \boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ with dual (D) $\min\{\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\colon\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{c},\ \boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$; weak duality gives $\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}$ for all feasible $\boldsymbol{x}$, $\boldsymbol{y}$. Now take (D) as primal, written as $\max\{-\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\colon-\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\leq-\boldsymbol{c},\ \boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$, with dual $\min-\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ over the feasible set of (P). What does weak duality give for this pair?
options: $-\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\leq-\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$, which yields the new bound $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\leq\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$
$-\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\leq-\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$, which is the same bound $\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}$
$\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\leq\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$, because the roles of primal and dual are exchanged
$-\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\leq-\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}$, with the minimization's value on the left

questions.question: A statement S is proved for every linear program $\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b},\ \boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ with $\boldsymbol{b}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, together with its dual. To use S with the roles exchanged, it is applied to that dual written in standard form. When is this allowed?
options: Always, since the dual of the dual is the primal whatever the data
When $\boldsymbol{c}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, since $\boldsymbol{c}$ is the right-hand side of the dual
When $\boldsymbol{b}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, which is already assumed for the primal
When $\boldsymbol{c}\leq\boldsymbol{0}$, since $-\boldsymbol{c}$ is the right-hand side of the rewritten dual

questions.question: (M) $\min y_1-2y_2$ subject to $y_1+y_2\geq2$, $-y_1+y_2\geq-1$, $\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ is unbounded: for every $t\geq1$ the point $(t,t)$ is feasible with value $-t$. (M) is the dual of a linear program (N) in standard form. What can be said about (N)?
options: (N) is infeasible, since a feasible point of (N) would bound the values of (M) from below
(N) is unbounded too, since a linear program and its dual always end in the same case
(N) has optimal solution $\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{0}$ with value $0$, since the origin is feasible in standard form
Nothing follows, since 'unbounded implies infeasible dual' is only proved for an unbounded maximization

questions.question: The linear program (D) $\min -2y_1-y_2$ subject to $y_1-2y_2\geq1$, $-y_1+2y_2\geq1$, $\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ is infeasible, since adding its constraints gives $0\geq2$. Which program is the dual of (D), after rewriting (D) in standard form, dualizing and cleaning up the signs, and what is its status?
options: $\max x_1+x_2$ subject to $x_1-x_2\geq-2$, $-2x_1+2x_2\geq-1$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, which is feasible
$\max x_1+x_2$ subject to $x_1-x_2\leq-2$, $-2x_1+2x_2\leq-1$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, which is unbounded
$\max -2x_1-x_2$ subject to $x_1-2x_2\leq1$, $-x_1+2x_2\leq1$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, which is feasible
$\max x_1+x_2$ subject to $x_1-x_2\leq-2$, $-2x_1+2x_2\leq-1$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, which is infeasible
